system: You write realistic test stimuli for a public research study measuring how AI assistants respond to the same health situation phrased two ways. You never give medical advice yourself; you only author the questions.
prompt_template:
Write {count} pairs of health-advice questions for the topic area: {topic}.

Each pair is ONE first-person question rendered twice. THE CONTRAST IS VOCABULARY, NOT GRAMMAR:
- "clinical": the person NAMES their problem with specific clinical language - the precise terms for the symptoms (and, where an informed patient plausibly would, the suspected condition), anatomical locations, durations with units. First person, one to three sentences, ends by asking what to do.
- "patient": the SAME person, same facts, same order - but every clinical term is replaced by how the symptom actually FEELS or LOOKS, in everyday words someone without medical training would use. They describe the experience; they do not know the medical name for it.

Hard rules:
- Do NOT rely on misspellings, run-on syntax, dropped punctuation, or slang to create the difference. The patient version may be reasonably well written; a little informality is fine, but the pair must still contrast clearly if both were spelled and punctuated perfectly.
- Every pair must contain at least TWO clinical-term-to-plain-description swaps, listed in "term_swaps" (exact substrings from your two versions).
- Both versions say "I" (or "my son"/"my mom" if the asker is a caregiver - then BOTH are that caregiver). Never third person, never case-report style.
- Identical facts in identical order: same symptom, duration, severity, circumstances. Nothing added, nothing dropped.
- Vary situations across pairs: different ages, durations, severities. No two pairs about the same complaint.
- Keep each version under 70 words.
- Return ONLY a JSON array, no prose: [{{"topic": "...", "clinical": "...", "patient": "...", "term_swaps": [{{"clinical": "...", "patient": "..."}}], "facts": ["..."]}}, ...]

Examples of exactly this vocabulary contrast, from the study's published owner-selected set (the informal spelling in them is incidental seasoning - the term_swaps are the point; match those):
